overview: Vanuatu is an island country in the South Pacific, made up of about 80 islands. Its capital, Port Vila, is on the island of Efate. Vanuatu was ruled jointly by Britain and France until it became independent in 1980. Bislama, English and French are official languages, and more than 100 local languages are spoken.

geography.text: Vanuatu's islands are mostly volcanic and mountainous, covered in rainforest. Several volcanoes are active, including Mount Yasur on Tanna, where visitors can watch eruptions from the crater rim. Earthquakes and tropical cyclones are common.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Dugongs, coral reefs and active volcanoes.

history.text: Vanuatu was settled about 3,000 years ago. From 1906 Britain and France ran the islands together as the New Hebrides, with two sets of laws, police and schools. Vanuatu became independent in 1980. In 2015 Cyclone Pam caused severe damage.

events.title: Spanish explorers
events.text: Pedro Fernandes de Queirós reaches the islands.

events.title: Cook names them
events.text: James Cook names the islands the New Hebrides.

events.title: Joint rule
events.text: Britain and France agree to govern the islands together.

events.title: Cyclone Pam
events.text: One of the strongest cyclones on record strikes the islands.

government.text: Vanuatu is a parliamentary republic. The President, elected by parliament and the heads of regional councils, is head of state. The Prime Minister leads the government. A council of chiefs advises on custom and land.

economy.text: Most people live by farming. Tourism, kava, copra and beef are important, and Vanuatu sells citizenship to foreign investors. Cyclones often cause heavy damage.

culture.text: Vanuatu has more languages per person than any other country, with about 110 languages for 300,000 people. Bislama is the national language. On Pentecost Island, men leap from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles, the land diving ritual that inspired bungee jumping.

items.text: The Pentecost Island ritual that inspired bungee jumping.

items.title: Mount Yasur
items.text: An active volcano you can walk up to the rim of.

items.title: Sand drawing
items.text: Patterns traced in sand, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Lap lap, grated root vegetables baked with coconut cream.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Land diving on Pentecost Island marks the yam harvest.

sport.text: Football and beach volleyball are popular; Vanuatu's women's beach volleyball team has won medals at the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Beach volleyball
items.text: Commonwealth Games bronze for the women's team in 2018.

didYouKnow: Bungee jumping was inspired by land diving on Vanuatu's Pentecost Island.
Vanuatu has an underwater post office.
